note: Signed human decisions. Every field the signature covers is at the top level; `context` is joined from the reservation for display and is NOT covered by the signature. 0 of 0 are lapses. A LAPSE HAS NO ACTOR AND IS STILL SIGNED: nobody acted, so there is no identity to attribute, and the deployment still attests that it saw the window elapse. Use `signedPayloadType` to know which bytes a signature covers — `op.approval.lapse.v1` is {type, handleId, at, expiresAt} and `op.approval.resolution.v1` is {type, handleId, how, at, actor, reason?}. On a lapse, `at` and `expiresAt` are DIFFERENT FACTS FROM DIFFERENT SOURCES and neither is derived from the other: `expiresAt` is when the approval window closed, from the handle, and `at` is when a sweep observed it, from the deployment clock. So `at` is LATER than `expiresAt` by up to one sweep interval, and that gap is the sweep cadence rather than a defect. Both are inside the signature. Use `signedBy` for the key a signature verifies against — one field on every row, so a verifier does not branch on `how` twice. It is a HINT about which key to try, not an assertion that the key is trustworthy. A lapse written before the key was captured has `signedBy: null` and is permanently unverifiable; that is an absence, never the current key. WARNING: `settle` records carry an unrelated field also named `how`, valued commit|release. Anything keying on `how` without keying on the record type will read a settlement as a resolution. Resolution `how` is one of: approved, denied, lapsed.
